Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *per-der.?

Latin prōdigiumlbor.
French prodige

    Learned borrowing from Latin prōdigium.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /pʁɔ.diʒ/
    • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)

    Noun

    [edit]

    prodige m (plural prodiges)

    1. prodigy, miracle
    2. prodigy (an extremely talented person, especially a child)

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • enfant prodige
    • prodigieux

    Further reading
